newsitem.title: TURKEY: Erbakan aide Turkey cabinet meeting goes ahead.
newsitem.headline: Erbakan aide Turkey cabinet meeting goes ahead.

text.p: An aide to Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said a cabinet meeting would go ahead on Tuesday despite an earlier report from his office that it had been postponed.
"The cabinet meeting is taking place at 1700 (1400 GMT)," Erbakan's press adviser Fikret Ozkan told Reuters. "The confusion was caused by a misunderstanding," he said.
A spokesman at Erbakan's office had said earlier that the meeting had been called off, amid a row between the coalition partners over Islamist activism.
The cabinet has not met for eight weeks in a deepening coalition rift between Erbakan's Islamists and the secularists of Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's True Path Party.
Ozkan said he would tell his press officer colleagues to announce that the meeting would take place. "I will give orders to my office now. They will make the necessary announcement," he said.
Army pressure on Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, has brought the 11-month-old coalition close to breaking point.
